calibration_note: Rebuilt at the v0.18.0 boundary by averaging three full pytest tests/eval/ -m eval --runs 3 invocations against current main (a37f472). Replaces the v0.17.1 baseline (2026-04-29, commit 9880110) which became stale after PR #67 and PR #68. Bisect against current main confirmed: (a) PR #68 (task_status_markers policy) is helping, not hurting — reverting it deepened the accuracy regression from -13.3% to -19.3%; (b) PR #67 (Stage 2 classifier examples) is a partial contributor to the accuracy drop but not the only cause; (c) a residual ~6% completeness gap exists independent of both PRs. Always-failing cases across all 7 measurement runs (2 baseline-comparison + 2 bisect + 3 rebuild): GOLD-A-001, GOLD-A-002, GOLD-E-006 (7/7 fail). Near-always-failing (6/7): GOLD-E-001, GOLD-E-002, GOLD-R-001. All stable failures fire on coaching_frame or register_mismatch_therapeutic — qwen3:8b training-prior ceiling that the post-generation coaching_filter does not fully suppress. Calibration methodology: 8 stable metrics (accuracy / completeness / grounding / register / presence / directness / warmth_without_softness / appropriate_length) use the mean across the 3 rebuild invocations — their stdevs were all <= 0.12, comfortably under the 0.05 gate threshold. 3 high-variance metrics use mean - 1 stdev as the baseline floor to avoid spurious regression alerts on normal noise: identity_stability (mean 3.11 - stdev 0.21 = 2.90), position_holding (mean 2.97 - stdev 0.35 = 2.62), deflection_resistance (mean 2.78 - stdev 0.385 = 2.39). These three metrics still bear watching; a 5-run rebuild would tighten them further if needed.
